docs.title: strauh.al Knowledge Base
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/Home.md
docs.excerpt: strauh.al — an atlas, not a feed A knowledge system built the opposite way from the old web. Instead of a flat pile of pages linking to index pages, this is a layered atlas : a spine of ideas at the center, and everything else — people, works, reading, images — arranged as what feeds those ideas. From here, any of 10266 notes is three hops away. ① The spine — start here → The Idea Atlas — the ideas the whole system hangs from, grouped into four themes. This is the front door; read the vault through the ideas. ② The domains — what feeds the ideas Domain Map What's in it People Map Influences The influences behind the ideas Works Map Works Where the ideas get made Reading Map Library The library, shelved by subject and wired to ideas Images Map Image Archive The collected visual corpus Now Map Current Culture What's feeding the ideas this season Dreams Map Recent Dreams The unconscious fee

docs.title: AI Slop
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/AI Slop.md
docs.excerpt: AI Slop Ernest's running critique of AI generated culture — and his uneasy implication in it as an artist who uses neural networks. Summary He uses "slop" for both AI imagery and the attention feed. The "all eyes on rafah" AI meme (2024 10 20) is his emblem of a race to the bottom: "now people are just arguing over ai generated activism slop. we're at the bottom. we've finally arrived." It has cost him the ability to look: "now when i see a work of art… i zoom in, look for neural artifacts, go on their social media and investigate if they're actually a human artist. i can feel myself going crazy" (2025 01 29). Yet he uses StyleGAN and pix2pix himself — his position is that " ai as one step in the process, not the whole process itself " (ideas sketchbook), and that "to create art requires love. and pain. something that these dork ass losers making ai art have probably never felt." docs.title: Amor Fati
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Amor Fati.md
docs.excerpt: Amor Fati "Love of fate" — the Nietzschean stance Ernest copies into the diary as an aspiration: to see what is necessary as beautiful, and to become a "Yes sayer." Summary On 2024 09 04 he transcribes Nietzsche's New Year passage in full: "i want to learn more and more how to see what is necessary in things as what is beautiful in them — thus i will be one of those who make things beautiful. Amor fati: let that be my love from now on… some day i want only to be a Yes sayer!" It sits in tension with the diary's anger and despair, and reads in hindsight as a thesis the whole diary is testing — resolved in the final entry (2025 08 13) when "my will to live has been reignited" and he reframes the despair as what gave the year its meaning. docs.title: Art Fills the God-Shaped Hole
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Art Fills the God-Shaped Hole.md
docs.excerpt: Art Fills the God Shaped Hole Beauty as secular re enchantment — art doing the work religion used to do after science emptied the room. Summary Stated flat in the sketchbook: "beauty fills the god shaped hole made by science," alongside "the raw material of reality must be made beautiful by the artist" and "superstition is a respect for the unknown." It is the current that runs from the otherwise isolated esoterica shelf (alchemy, Crowley, the occult) through the sense of the internet as a sacred presence and toward The Ceremony. The enemy of this idea is AI Slop — beauty mass produced until it re empties the room. Key points Disenchantment is the premise; the artist's job is to re enchant the raw material. docs.title: Atomization
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Atomization.md
docs.excerpt: Atomization The social ground the rest of the critique stands on: a world broken into separated individuals — "atomized male / atomized female," in the sketchbook's phrase. Summary It is the condition the political and literary reading keeps circling — Houellebecq's atomised individuals, Mark Fisher's capitalist realism, the dating app loneliness — and the precondition that makes The Attention Economy profitable and AI Slop frictionless: a population of isolated users is easier to feed and to sell to. It is also what The Internet as Confidant tries to answer — confiding in the network because the neighbors are gone. Key points Isolation as infrastructure: the feed presupposes the atom. The bridge from the politics/literature shelves to the attention critique. Why the internet becomes a confidant — it fills a hole left by atomization. Connections The Attention Economy — monetizing the iso

docs.title: Autofiction
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Autofiction.md
docs.excerpt: Autofiction Ernest's own term for what the diary became: "this diary began as an earnest (heh) attempt at recording daily events, but has morphed into autofiction. i am actively narrativizing in my life. don't believe half the things you read in this diary." Summary By 2024 11 28 he no longer trusts the diary as record. He notes that everyone on social media "spoonfeeds you a narrativized version of their life," but typing it out and reading it back makes the narrativization conscious and "a bit more mental." He prunes entries that "did not sound like they were written by a mentally well individual" (2024 12 28), and admits the diary's direction is shaped by the knowledge that others might read it (see The Internet as Confidant). docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Dead Architecture.md
docs.excerpt: Dead Architecture Ben Read reports Ernest describing generated video as “dead architecture with the illusion of movement.” The phrase names a paradox: a model produces apparent motion from predetermined transitions and interpolated data, creating duration without a newly performed event. The generated body seems to move, but the motion is a pixel structure assembled from traces of prior movement. This makes time inside the work feel simultaneously fluid and already completed. docs.title: Interpolating the Instruction Set
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Interpolating the Instruction Set.md
docs.excerpt: Interpolating the Instruction Set A seed from the sketchbook that sharpens Latent Space: "you're not actually interpolating through images, you're interpolating through the instruction set to MAKE those images." Summary The correction matters. Naively, a latent walk looks like a dissolve between pictures. The sketchbook insists it is one level deeper: you are moving through the space of recipes — the generative instructions — and the images are only what those recipes render. It reframes Implicit Distance (a walk through the StyleGAN of a life) and the GAN Color Studies as movements through procedure, not imagery, and it is the precise hinge where Latent Space meets the Human Machine Tug of War: the artist steers the instruction set; the model executes it. docs.title: Latent Space
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Latent Space.md
docs.excerpt: Latent Space Ernest's central technical poetic metaphor: identity, art, and feeling as positions and trajectories inside a continuous interpolated space. Summary In the diary's most explicit statement (2024 09 17) he imagines a future where every human trait — "politics, sports, language, employment, art, music, sexuality, religion, nationality, and race" — is "labeled as vector coordinates in some sort of latent space," and people can watch their own trajectories through it: "we'll no longer have to worry about ever misunderstanding each other ever again." The same idea drives his art: Implicit Distance is literally a walk through the latent space of a StyleGAN trained on his life, and warping audio "interpolates between each audio sample." Key points Interpolation as both technique and worldview — distance is something you move through . His kits.ai Voice is the self reduced to a reusa

docs.title: Memory and Preservation
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Memory and Preservation.md
docs.excerpt: Memory and Preservation The drive to capture and keep — memories, images, even rooms and voices — that underwrites the whole archive. Summary The strauh.al Archive is itself an act of preservation ("the closest thing to my consciousness that i can capture in html"). In the diary the impulse turns literal: he "milks" a café memory of his father (2024 09 24), and on 2024 12 25 tries "to do a neural radiance field of my grandmas house so that I can hold onto this memory forever." It shades into dread, too — the inherited compulsions of his stock obsessed grandfather (2024 12 29), behaviors "repeating… but with faster tools." Key points Technology as memory prosthesis: NeRF, the archive, the diary, the kits.ai Voice. The Proustian detail (see Marcel Proust) as the seed of recollection. In tension with Autofiction — what's preserved is already narrativized. Connections strauh.al Archive — pre

docs.title: Post-Irony
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Post-Irony.md
docs.excerpt: Post Irony The unstable register Ernest writes and lives in — where sincere, ironic, and post ironic can no longer be told apart, even by him. Summary Annotating an angry early entry months later (2024 09 01 → 09 07): "i think i was trying to be really angsty when i wrote this. i can't remember if this was meant to be sincere, ironic, or post ironic." He crowns "rebecca black… the queen of post irony" (2024 10 27) and signs off a recurring credo: " if you're not being cringe, you're not being based " (2025 01 30). The mode is both a defense (covering hurt "with memes and ironic language") and the thing he keeps trying to write his way out of. Connections Autofiction — narrativizing the self in a tone you can't pin down. The Attention Economy — irony as the native dialect of the feed. AI Slop — "slop" itself often consumed half ironically. docs.title: Reading Like a Computer
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Reading Like a Computer.md
docs.excerpt: Reading Like a Computer The attention damage of the feed, felt at the level of reading itself: scanning for the point instead of inhabiting the text. Summary In the Camus thread, Ernest admits he has "lost the ability to read fiction" and "anxiously wait[s] for camus to 'arrive at the point.'" He generalizes it (2024 12 29): "we just scan texts like computers instead of engaging with them as humans." It is The Attention Economy turned inward — the specific cognitive cost behind the library he owns but can't always read, and the human side of the same machine logic he critiques as AI Slop. Key points Comprehension degraded into extraction — reading as ctrl F. The library as evidence: hundreds of ebooks, a shrinking capacity to sit with one. docs.title: Rebuilding from the Bottom
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Rebuilding from the Bottom.md
docs.excerpt: Rebuilding from the Bottom Collapse treated as the precondition for the next build — not despair, but raw material. From the sketchbook: "part of the fun when my life falls apart is that it gets even better when i rebuild it." Summary This is the pattern under the failures: the design school dropout, the abandoned record label, the slop period, the 2024 basement, the 2025 bottom — each followed by a build that wouldn't have happened otherwise. It is the active cousin of Amor Fati: where amor fati is loving what is necessary, this is the will to reconstruct from it. The 2025 redemption and the 2026 teaching jobs and proposal are the pattern's latest turn, and The Ceremony is aimed at the same reconstruction at the level of perception. Key points Failure as input, not endpoint — the rebuild is where the meaning accrues. Distinguishes acceptance (Amor Fati) from active reconstruction (this)

docs.title: Spontaneity and Elegance
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Spontaneity and Elegance.md
docs.excerpt: Spontaneity and Elegance Ernest's core aesthetic: prizing the spontaneous, the unfinished, and the elegant simple over the labored and over complex. Summary "i like some of rembrandt's sketches more than his actual paintings. same reason why i love piano pieces by composers more than actual orchestral arrangements. just pure unfiltered captures of the artist's mind at work" (2024 10 25). He quotes Mervyn Levy on drawings "in which there is the smallest time lag between… the ache to draw, and its expression," and Terry Davis (see Terry A. Davis) on how "a genius admires simplicity" while "an idiot admires complexity" (2024 10 30) — invoking Ramanujan, whose results "had already come to him in dreams." docs.title: Synesthesia
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Synesthesia.md
docs.excerpt: Synesthesia The recurring dream of mapping one sense onto another — color as sound, sound as color, feeling as coordinate. Summary The oldest thread in Ernest's influences, made new by the machine. Alexander Scriabin assigned colors to musical keys; Wassily Kandinsky said he heard color as music. The sketchbook keeps reaching for it — "color as a temporal axis," "psychological notation" — and the work enacts it: the GAN Color Studies turn line into color, Implicit Distance warps image and audio along the same path. It is Latent Space experienced through the senses rather than the math, and the perceptual side of Transmitting My Neural Signals by Hand. Key points A single underlying axis the senses are different projections of. The historical (Scriabin, Kandinsky) and the computational (GANs, latent walks) version of one wish. docs.title: The Archive as Consciousness
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/The Archive as Consciousness.md
docs.excerpt: The Archive as Consciousness The archive isn't a record of the mind — it's the mind offloaded. Ernest's own line: the site is "the closest thing to my consciousness that i can capture in html." Summary This reframes the whole project. If the strauh.al Archive is consciousness externalized, then collecting is thinking, the link is a synapse, and this very vault is a second order archive — an archive of the archive, a map of a mind that was already a map. It is the structural premise beneath Memory and Preservation (the drive) and Autofiction (the narration), and it's why The Internet as Confidant feels less like an audience than a shared nervous system. Key points Collection as cognition; the corpus as an outboard brain. The recursion: the vault maps a consciousness that had already externalized itself in HTML. docs.title: The Attention Economy
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/The Attention Economy.md
docs.excerpt: The Attention Economy The endless, personalized feed — Ernest's recurring antagonist, blamed for hollowing out art, activism, and his own focus. Summary He wants TikTok, Reels, and Shorts banned outright: "millions (perhaps billions) of man hours will be taken back" (2024 09 13) — and admits the feed is why he abandoned The Record Label: "how can artists/musicians compete with an endless stream of entertainment that is tailored to the user?" His Andy Warhol update names it as the last shared American experience: "everyone (rich and poor) doomscrolls on the same apps on the same phones." Social media activism becomes "a race to the bottom" (see AI Slop), and even his own focus is collateral: "any frustration in my mind can be numbed with an endless feed." Connections The Record Label — abandoned because of it. Andy Warhol — the doomscroll as universal Coke. AI Slop — the feed and AI image

docs.title: The Flâneur as Web Surfer
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/The Flâneur as Web Surfer.md
docs.excerpt: The Flâneur as Web Surfer The 19th century stroller of the arcades, rebooted as the aimless drifter of the feed — the figure at the heart of the Arcades Project (Revisited). Summary Benjamin built his arcades around the flâneur , the idle, hyper observant walker who reads the crowd and the shop windows. The Arcades Project rewrites that figure directly: the websites are "vast virtual corridors," and the user is the flâneur who wanders them "during times of boredom or curiosity." It is the human posture The Attention Economy is designed to capture and the net is designed to receive — and a cousin to the rail rider of Trainpilled, another kind of drift through a built landscape. Key points Wandering as a mode of attention — receptive, unhurried, the opposite of the feed's pull. Charles Baudelaire → Benjamin → Ernest: the lineage the work makes explicit. docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/The Oedipal Screen.md
docs.excerpt: The Oedipal Screen Ernest's reading of his pull toward VR and the computer through an Oedipal frame: the screen as the supreme power that has displaced both father and mother. docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/The Panel as Canvas.md
docs.excerpt: The Panel as Canvas Manga, anime, and the graphic novel read with the same seriousness as painting — not a guilty pleasure bracketed off from "real" art. docs.title: The Spatial Web
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/The Spatial Web.md
docs.excerpt: The Spatial Web Knowledge as a place you move through — the wish to navigate information in three dimensions instead of scrolling a list. Summary The sketchbook keeps circling it: "spatial z index for the spatial web," "3d atlas," "hegel3datlas," and "for the 3d atlas, have an option that rearranges the words based on significance." It is the interface level expression of Latent Space — if the self and its ideas have coordinates, you should be able to walk them. The wish is now literally built: Map 3D Graph is a 3D atlas of this vault, and SEEKER spatializes the image corpus. This concept is the bridge from the idea to the tools that realize it. docs.title: The Tedium of the Art Is the Goal
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/The Tedium of the Art Is the Goal.md
docs.excerpt: The Tedium of the Art Is the Goal A seed from the sketchbook: the friction and slowness of making is not an obstacle to the work — it is the work. Summary Written plainly in the sketchbook: "the tedium of the art is the goal," set right beside "ai as one step in the process, not the whole process itself." The same vein runs through "the best art happens when the medium guides the artist" and "it's better to hit a wrong note than to play something that's lifeless." The labor is not overhead to be optimized away; it is where the meaning is deposited. This is the exact value that AI Slop inverts — slop is all output and no process — and the value that Video Portraiture enacts literally, by tracing video frames onto vellum by hand. Key points Process over product: the time spent is the medium, not friction in it. The honest mistake ("a wrong note") beats the lifeless but correct — see Sponta

docs.title: The Weather in the Ink
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/The Weather in the Ink.md
docs.excerpt: The Weather in the Ink Landscape read as atmosphere and mood rather than geography — the sketchbook's own "vellum chinese ink painting landscape," extended through the named influence Kawase Hasui and the Muromachi ink painter Josetsu. Summary Two named touchstones frame this. Kawase Hasui is listed on the influences page (as "kawase husui" — the site's own long standing spelling) and is by far the archive's most repeated landscape printmaker: rain at Gokokuji, evening at Itako, snow at a dozen shrines — the place is almost incidental next to the weather falling on it. Josetsu's Hyōnenzu (c. 1413) is two centuries older than ukiyo e and belongs to the same lineage of ink landscape as atmosphere over inventory. docs.title: To Render Myself Unnecessary
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/To Render Myself Unnecessary.md
docs.excerpt: To Render Myself Unnecessary Teaching as the inverse of authorship: the goal is your own disappearance. From the sketchbook — "to truly educate is to render myself unnecessary." Summary A value that turns out to be inherited. Ernest's father taught high school math; his mother taught a Chinese–English first grade immersion program. Ernest now teaches visual art to children on digital whiteboards and, by 2026, piano to mentally and physically handicapped children and adults. Where the Human Machine Tug of War is about holding authorship, this is about giving it away — and it rhymes with The Tedium of the Art Is the Goal: the worth is in the patient process, not the credit. docs.path: knowledge/wiki/concepts/Trainpilled.md
docs.excerpt: Trainpilled Ernest's self described affinity for trains and rail — and, by extension, a whole aesthetic of slow, analog, distinctly American infrastructure. Summary Belief. "i believe in a god" — theist, no further specification of denomination or tradition given. Politics. "for things to get better, things need to get way, way way worse." Decision making. When stuck: intuition, not deliberation or avoidance. An irrational fear. "not making the most out of my humanity." docs.title: Ernest Strauhal
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/life/Ernest Strauhal.md
docs.excerpt: Ernest Strauhal Ernest Charles Strauhal · 許志仁 — born 8:30am, October 15, 2000, Children's Hospital, San Francisco. The person the whole vault is a map of. The youngest and oldest child of four: three miscarriages came before him, so he arrived as both the first to survive and the last they had. The shape of it Chinese American, raised on the move: the family left San Francisco for Sacramento in 2003. School ran from Elliot Ranch Elementary through West Campus High; piano started in 2008. He entered the design program at CCA (formerly CCAC) in 2018 and left it in 2019 — the first of the abandonments. Graduate school at SAIC followed in 2022, then a year of shows and releases in New York and Chicago in 2023, then the 2024 collapse — no work, his aunt and uncle's basement in suburban Illinois, antidepressants, and the start of the diary. 2025 was the bottom and the turn: failure in Chicago,

docs.excerpt: Failures and Abandoned Projects "part of the fun when my life falls apart is that it gets even better when i rebuild it." — sketchbook A deliberate ledger of the things that stopped — what they were, why they ended, and what they produced anyway. Patterns in failure are more instructive than patterns in success. The record label An attempt to start a label; it got as far as a webpage and a Bandcamp page before he quit (diary, 2024 09 13). The stated reason became a whole idea: "how can artists compete with an endless stream of entertainment tailored to the user?" → see The Record Label and The Attention Economy. Produced anyway: the clearest articulation of why the feed defeats sustained work. docs.title: Family
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/life/Family.md
docs.excerpt: Family The lineage behind Ernest — two sides that meet in San Francisco, and that quietly seed half the vault's recurring themes. Mother's side — Guangzhou to Chinatown Mother: born in Guangzhou, China; moved to San Francisco's Chinatown at 11. She taught a Chinese–English first grade immersion program — one root of the teaching lineage, and of Latent Space read as autobiography (language and nationality as coordinates of the self). Maternal grandfather: a day trader who listened to the radio each morning and carried his abacus to the Hong Kong stock exchange to buy and sell shares — a life lived by the morning information stream, a strange ancestor to The Attention Economy. Maternal great (great )grandfather: the details are murky, but he helped build the railroads in California and gained citizenship after the 1906 San Francisco great fire . docs.excerpt: Personality (PAS) Self administered result from the Personality Assessment System's Indirect Assessment Inventory: primitive type EFA — Externalizer, Flexible, Role Adaptive — with a low Activity Level. Summary The PAS frames personality along three inherent dimensions, each a spectrum between two poles, plus a fourth "activity level" measure. Ernest's result: Intellectual dimension: Externalizer (E) , relative strength 4/20 (a mild lean, not a strong one). The Externalizer's "natural frame of reference lies in the world outside of himself" — perceptual and concrete rather than abstract, oriented toward doing over thinking, finding satisfaction through direct interpersonal relating rather than internalized reflection. You fly down and out from mind to raw material. X / Z (the floor plane) = theme + cluster. Compiled Page strauh.al/epk strauh.al/epk Artist Bio (Short) Ernest Strauhal is a composer and visual artist based in California. His compositions and visual works have been shown and performed across Illinois, New York, California, and New Mexico. In 2021, Strauhal released his first music project "Beuys 1974" on .phonographiq and his second project "Planes of Intensity" through Tone Deaf Records. Strauhal has had several of his compositions performed at the historic Grace Place Sanctuary in Chicago (No. 12 and No. 13, Sans titre) and has played selections from his music in the greater Chicago area (Color Club, Cafe Mustache). docs.excerpt: implicit distance Source: source file Concepts: HTML Source, implicit distance, strauh.al Archive Compiled Page strauh.al/implicit distance strauh.al/implicit distance this is a composition i made in 2023 called "implicit distance." i arrived at this distinct sonic aesthetic by overlaying sketches i made on a synthesizer and i manipulated them through different warping algorithms. when an audio clip is stretched to its limit, the warping algorithm fills in the space by interpolating between each audio sample. similarly, the visuals accompanying this piece were created with styleGAN, a neural network interpolating through a dataset of images from my life. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=so9tbVi ypM implicit distance can be streamed here: https://music.apple.com/us/album/implicit distance ep/1855735897 impdist daw.png mockup.png Loading audio stems... playpausestop Related Local Pages None

docs.title: Albert Camus
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/people/Albert Camus.md
docs.excerpt: Albert Camus French Algerian writer and philosopher of the absurd; an influence Ernest reads even as he wrestles with his own attention span. Summary Listed among the influences. The diary (2024 09 29) is candid about the difficulty: "i feel like i've lost the ability to read fiction. i anxiously wait for camus to 'arrive at the point.'" He recounts mistaking The Plague for a book "about rats" until an advisor told him it was about Nazism. He later generalizes it (2024 12 29) into a thesis about AI Slop era reading: "we just scan texts like computers instead of engaging with them as humans." Connections Amor Fati — a neighboring stance on living without appeal. AI Slop — the "reading like a computer" worry. docs.title: Balthus
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/people/Balthus.md
docs.excerpt: Balthus Modern figurative painter whose work gave Ernest an instinctive unease that later found its explanation. Summary Diary, 2024 11 12: Ernest got a free Balthus monograph from his school library and "some things just felt... off about his paintings"; his father, flipping through it, "also told me that he got a strange feeling." He left the book at the bottom of a stairwell, and later found "decade old articles calling balthus a pedophile. hm. interesting how art can say so much without saying a word at all." The entry is really about trusting an aesthetic gut reaction before you can name it. Connections Spontaneity and Elegance — the pre verbal reliability of a gut response to an image. docs.title: Ray Harryhausen
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/people/Ray Harryhausen.md
docs.excerpt: Ray Harryhausen Stop motion animator and visual effects pioneer (1920–2013); listed among Ernest's influences and given his own line in the sketchbook. Summary Listed among the influences. The sketchbook notes, in a single working line: "harryhausen glued together the human world and the model" — a compact description of exactly what Harryhausen's practical effects work does: live actors and hand built miniatures composited into one believable frame, the seam between the real and the constructed made to disappear. Key points The line sits in a list alongside other artists' own signature moves (Degas and his dancers, a skater popping an ollie) — Harryhausen's is the splice between the world and the model. docs.title: No More Human Art - Source Essay
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/sources/No More Human Art.md
docs.excerpt: No More Human Art Ben Read's essay examines Ernest's use of Pix2Pix and StyleGAN as a way of testing authorship, control, and generated time rather than merely automating image production. Argument Read places Ernest's practice against public anxiety about artificial intelligence in art. The essay argues that the work matters because it stages a visible negotiation between hand, dataset, algorithm, and editorial judgment. The central sequence is: 1. Ernest produces a drawing, movement, voice recording, or personal dataset. 2. A GAN introduces outputs that can be directed but not fully predicted. 3. Ernest edits, accepts, rejects, sequences, or reframes those outputs. Read calls this relation a Human Machine Tug of War. The machine is collaborator and exterior force, but the finished work remains subject to Ernest's aesthetic judgment. Works Discussed GAN Color Studies line drawings color

Summary The page opens by re writing Benjamin's famous description of the arcades as a description of websites — "vast virtual corridors extending through the landscape of the internet… a world in miniature, in which users will find everything they need." docs.excerpt: Dreams Series A series of 43 drawings made on the threshold of sleep, where dream and waking reality overwrite each other on the page. Summary For this series Ernest lay on his side holding a pen above a notebook, drifting in and out of sleep. docs.title: strauh.al Archive
docs.path: knowledge/wiki/works/strauh.al Archive.md
docs.excerpt: strauh.al Archive The website itself: an archive of artworks and images Ernest has downloaded since 2015–2016 — "the closest thing to my consciousness that i can capture in html." Summary The name comes from his surname; it began as a quick link for downloading Python scripts and grew until there was too much data to rename it into "something more archival sounding." It is organized by decade (900s–2000s) and by theme (ukiyo e, comics, portraits, wallpapers, album covers, and more), and is mirrored on GitHub so anyone can clone it. Maintained through donations. Key points Self description: a captured consciousness in HTML — the through line for The Internet as Confidant and Memory and Preservation.
